topic.title: Language-Model Security and Adversarial Evaluation
topic.overview: Language-model security studies how adversarial inputs, hidden triggers, and external information can redirect system behavior. This cluster includes prompt defenses, adaptive red teaming, backdoor attribution, and attacks on automated judges. The unit of evaluation increasingly extends beyond a standalone response to the workflows through which a model retrieves, evaluates, and cites information.
topic.whyItMatters: A model can appear safe under standard prompts yet fail after targeted adaptation or tool use. Defenses must preserve legitimate information while testing the particular access and feedback available to an adversary.
topic.evolution: Early representatives examine prompt backdoors and fitting-based defenses. The 2024–2025 work develops information-bottleneck protection, adversarial tuning, and adaptive prompt evaluation. Recent examples expose judge-style manipulation and web-search citation risks, illustrating why security tests need to follow the deployed system’s full information path.
openQuestions: How can defense evaluations remain valid against adaptive rather than fixed attacks?
Which workflow-level safeguards preserve useful retrieval without trusting adversarial external content?

papers.tldr: CircuitPrint uses query-visible signatures of stable internal computations to verify model identity without modifying parameters.

papers.title: D-Judge: Disrupting Multi-Turn Jailbreaks using Semantics-Preserving Output Rewriting
papers.tldr: D-Judge preserves response meaning while rewriting wording to disrupt the feedback that guides multi-turn jailbreak attacks.

papers.title: Detecting Fluent Optimization-Based Adversarial Prompts via Sequential Entropy Changes
papers.tldr: A training-free detector tracks sequential entropy changes to identify fluent adversarial suffixes and localize where they begin.

papers.title: Disentangling Intent from Role: Adversarial Self-Play for Persona-Invariant Safety Alignment
papers.tldr: PIA uses adversarial self-play and consistency learning to reduce persona-based jailbreak success while preserving general model capability.

papers.title: Does AI Reviewer See the Full Picture? Attacking and Defending Multimodal Peer Review
papers.tldr: PaperGuard benchmarks attacks through paper text and figures and introduces a chunk-search defense for automated peer review.

papers.title: Efficient Code Analysis via Graph Representation Learning-Guided Large Language Models
papers.tldr: A graph neural network identifies suspicious code regions and directs a language model toward cross-file malicious behavior.

papers.title: Eyes-on-Me: Scalable RAG Poisoning through Transferable Attention-Steering Attractors
papers.tldr: Eyes-on-Me shows that reusable attention-steering components can make RAG poisoning more transferable and substantially increase attack success.

papers.title: FLIPS: Instance-Fingerprinting for LLMs via Pseudo-random Sequences
papers.tldr: FLIPS uses biases in generated binary sequences to distinguish deployed LLM configurations, achieving high identification accuracy across 237 instances.

papers.title: From Poisoned to Aware: Fostering Backdoor Self-Awareness in LLMs
papers.tldr: The framework trains poisoned language models to articulate hidden backdoor triggers and uses that information for detection and mitigation.

papers.title: From Prompts to Responses: Dual-Sided Data Leakage and Defense in Split Large Language Models
papers.tldr: The paper exposes prompt and response leakage in split LLMs and introduces a defense with strong empirical protection and minimal task-performance impact.

papers.title: Furina: Fragmented Uncertainty-Driven Refusal Instability Attack
papers.tldr: Furina links jailbreak vulnerability to unstable refusal behavior marked by greater output uncertainty and weaker internal safety activation.

papers.title: Greedy Coordinate Diffusion: Effective and Semantically Coherent Adversarial Attacks via Diffusion Guidance
papers.tldr: Diffusion-guided adversarial prompts combine strong reported attack success with coherent language and lower detection rates under the tested filters.

papers.title: Hair-Trigger Alignment: Black-Box Evaluation Cannot Guarantee Post-Update Alignment
papers.tldr: Passing static black-box alignment tests cannot guarantee that a model remains aligned after even a benign update.

papers.title: Hearing Without Noticing? Attention-Aware Stealthy Black-Box Adversarial Audio Attacks
papers.tldr: Attention-aware objectives and music selection make tested adversarial audio more effective and less noticeable to listeners.

papers.title: Hide and Seek in Embedding Space: Geometry-based Steganography and Detection in Large Language Models
papers.tldr: Embedding-based secret encodings reduce classifier recoverability while improving secret transmission, and internal probes reveal potential detection signals.

papers.title: INDEXGUARD: Index-only Backdoor Vetting for Secure Federated PEFT of Large Language Models
papers.tldr: IndexGuard screens federated fine-tuning clients for backdoors using overlap among salient update indices without inspecting update values.

papers.title: Jailbreak Foundry: From Papers to Runnable Attacks for Reproducible Benchmarking
papers.tldr: Jailbreak Foundry turns attack papers into reusable executable modules and standardizes their evaluation to support continually updated robustness benchmarks.

papers.title: Jailbreak to Protect: Buffering and Reinforcing via Temporary Jailbreaking for Safe Fine-Tuning in Large Language Models
papers.tldr: Buffer-and-Reinforce uses a temporary jailbreak adapter to reduce harmful fine-tuning updates, then merges in an adapter that strengthens refusal behavior.

papers.title: Lookahead-GCG: Improving Universal Multi-Model Optimization-Based Jailbreaking Attacks via Stochastic Nesterov Optimization
papers.tldr: Lookahead-GCG improves reported jailbreak transferability by stabilizing adversarial prompt optimization across multiple surrogate models.

papers.title: Making Models Unmergeable via Scaling-Sensitive Loss Landscape
papers.tldr: Trap² trains weights to remain useful alone but degrade under rescaling that often accompanies unauthorized model merging.

papers.title: MemPot: Defending Against Memory Extraction Attack with Optimized Honeypots
papers.tldr: MemPot uses optimized memory honeypots and sequential evidence gathering to detect extraction attacks while preserving tested agent utility.

papers.title: Metis: Learning to Jailbreak LLMs via Self-Evolving Metacognitive Policy Optimization
papers.tldr: Metis uses feedback-driven policy optimization for red teaming, reporting high attack success and lower token costs across ten tested models.

papers.title: MultiBreak: A Scalable and Diverse Multi-turn Jailbreak Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Safety
papers.tldr: MultiBreak provides a large, diverse conversational jailbreak benchmark that exposes vulnerabilities missed by single-turn evaluations.

papers.title: New Wide-Net-Casting Jailbreak Attacks Risk Large Models
papers.tldr: Querying groups of models creates a distinct jailbreak risk, with a tailored attack reaching 100% success in some experiments without additional safeguards.

papers.title: No More, No Less: Least-Privilege Language Models
papers.tldr: Least-privilege language models restrict reachable internal computation per request, enabling reversible capability control with measured utility tradeoffs.

papers.title: OrchJail: Jailbreaking Tool-Calling Text-to-Image Agents by Orchestration-Guided Fuzzing
papers.tldr: OrchJail studies safety failures caused by multi-step image-tool orchestration and improves their discovery in the reported evaluations.

papers.title: OSCS: Online Selection with Provable FAR Control for LLM Safety
papers.tldr: OSCS uses streaming detection scores to control false acceptance up to a vanishing excess term under mild assumptions, without malicious calibration data.

papers.title: Poison with Style: A Practical Poisoning Attack on Code Large Language Models
papers.tldr: Poison-with-Style uses developers’ coding styles as covert triggers for vulnerable code generation while largely preserving ordinary completion performance.

papers.title: Position: Generative Distributional Integrity against Backdoor Attacks
papers.tldr: The paper proposes Distributional Integrity to address generative backdoors across model supply chains and synthetic-data pipelines.

papers.title: Prompt Injection as Role Confusion
papers.tldr: The paper links prompt-injection success to measurable role confusion, where models internally treat untrusted text as the trusted source it imitates.

papers.title: Rapid Poison: Practical Poisoning Attacks Against the Rapid Response Framework
papers.tldr: The paper shows that poisoning attack-derived synthetic data can make adaptive jailbreak detectors reject harmless inputs or accept triggered jailbreaks.

papers.title: REALISTA: Realistic Latent Adversarial Attacks that Elicit LLM Hallucinations
papers.tldr: REALISTA searches continuous combinations of valid rephrasing directions to find realistic prompts that elicit hallucinations.

papers.title: Reasoning as an Attack Surface: Adaptive Evolutionary CoT Jailbreaks for LLMs
papers.tldr: AE-CoT uses adaptive evolutionary search over reasoning-based attacks and outperforms existing jailbreak methods across the evaluated models and datasets.

papers.title: RedVisor: Reasoning-Aware Prompt Injection Defense via Zero-Copy KV Cache Reuse
papers.tldr: RedVisor uses a temporary reasoning adapter to detect prompt injections and guide safe responses while reusing cached computation.

papers.title: Reflector: Internalizing Step-wise Reflection against Indirect Jailbreaks
papers.tldr: Reflector trains step-wise self-reflection, reporting over 90% defense success against complex indirect attacks alongside utility gains.

papers.title: Reranker Helps, but Not Enough: Towards Strong Poisoning Attacks Against Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.tldr: Rerankers filter many poisoned documents, but P3A shows that small textual perturbations can preserve attacks while improving their ranking.

papers.title: Reverse-Engineering Model Editing on Language Models
papers.tldr: KSTER recovers edited information from model-update structure, while a proposed camouflage defense reduces this leakage without harming editing utility.

papers.title: Reward Under Attack: Analyzing the Robustness and Hackability of Process Reward Models
papers.tldr: Adversarial tests show that process reward models can assign very high rewards to incorrect reasoning, making them exploitable training signals.

papers.title: Robust Harmful Features Under Jailbreak Attacks: Mechanistic Evidence from Attention Head Specialization in Large Language Models
papers.tldr: The paper finds that jailbreaks can suppress refusal-related attention heads while leaving persistent internal safety signals useful for detection.

papers.title: SARSteer: Safeguarding Large Audio Language Models via Safe-Ablated Refusal Steering
papers.tldr: SARSteer adapts refusal steering for audio-language models to improve harmful-query rejection while preserving responses to benign speech.

papers.title: SecCodePRM: A Process Reward Model for Code Security
papers.tldr: SecCodePRM scores security throughout code generation, improving vulnerability detection and secure continuation selection while preserving evaluated functional correctness.

papers.title: Security–Fidelity Tradeoffs: The Hidden Cost of Prompt Injection Defense
papers.tldr: SecFid shows that prompt-injection defenses can gain security by dropping required content, exposing a deployment-dependent tradeoff with fidelity.

papers.title: “Someone Hid It!”: Query-Agnostic Black-Box Attacks on LLM-Based Retrieval
papers.tldr: Transferable document injections manipulate tested language-model retrievers without knowing victim queries or accessing the victim model.

papers.title: SPARD: Defending Harmful Fine-Tuning Attack via Safety Projection with Relevance–Diversity Data Selection
papers.tldr: SPARD combines alternating safety projections with relevant, diverse safe-data selection to defend against harmful fine-tuning while preserving task accuracy.

papers.title: SpatialJB: How Text Distribution Art Becomes The "Jailbreak Key" for LLM Guardrails
papers.tldr: SpatialJB exposes experimentally strong jailbreak vulnerabilities involving spatial text structure and evaluates baseline defenses against them.

papers.title: Speech-Audio Compositional Attacks on Multimodal LLMs and Their Defense with SALMONN-Guard
papers.tldr: SACRED-Bench exposes safety failures in composed audio inputs, while SALMONN-Guard reduces reported attack success from 66% to 20%.

papers.title: Steering Beyond the Support: Adversarial Training on Unsupervised Jailbroken Activation Simulation
papers.tldr: The method trains a safety-steering defense on simulated jailbroken activations discovered without knowledge of specific jailbreak strategies.

papers.title: Structured Multi-step Jailbreaking under a Hamiltonian Generative Formulation
papers.tldr: SJA uses a hyperbolic Hamiltonian formulation to study structured multi-step jailbreaks that preserve harmful meaning across individually harmless sub-questions.

papers.title: TCAP: Tri-Component Attention Profiling for Unsupervised Backdoor Detection in MLLM Fine-Tuning
papers.tldr: TCAP detects poisoned multimodal fine-tuning samples by profiling shifts in attention across instructions, images, and user text.

papers.title: Through the Stealth Lens: Attention-Aware Defenses Against Poisoning in RAG
papers.tldr: Attention-based passage scoring detects influential RAG poisoning and improves robustness, though adaptive attacks retain reported success.

papers.title: TokenSwap: Backdoor Attack on the Compositional Understanding of Large Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: TokenSwap implants a stealthy backdoor that preserves object names but corrupts their relationships in vision-language model outputs.

papers.title: TraceRouter: Robust Safety for Large Foundation Models via Path-Level Intervention
papers.tldr: TraceRouter traces and suppresses cross-layer pathways carrying harmful information, improving the reported balance between robustness and utility.

papers.title: Tracing the Dynamics of Refusal: Exploiting Latent Refusal Trajectories for Robust Jailbreak Detection
papers.tldr: SALO detects jailbreaks by monitoring internal refusal trajectories that often persist after attacks suppress final refusal signals.

papers.title: Training with Honeypots: Reshaping How LLMs Fail Under Adversarial Attacks
papers.tldr: Honeypot-inspired safety training aims to make adversarial failures less actionable while reducing the frequency of harmful responses.

papers.title: Trojan-Speak: Bypassing Constitutional Classifiers with No Jailbreak Tax via Adversarial Finetuning
papers.tldr: Trojan-Speak demonstrates high classifier evasion with limited reasoning degradation, while activation-level probes improve robustness to the studied attacks.

papers.title: Turning Bias into Bugs: Bandit-Guided Style Manipulation Attacks on LLM Judges
papers.tldr: BITE adaptively selects meaning-preserving style edits that exploit LLM judges’ biases and inflate evaluation scores.

papers.title: Uncovering Hidden Triggers: Backdoor Attribution in Language Models
papers.tldr: BkdAttr identifies sparse attention heads involved in backdoors and derives representation interventions that strongly control attack success in experiments.

papers.title: When Search Goes Wrong: Red-Teaming Web-Augmented Large Language Models
papers.tldr: CREST-Search reveals safety weaknesses in web-enabled LLMs by testing whether benign-looking queries can induce unsafe citations.
